findings.problem: The cost comparison is text and numbers, not a picture. 'wrap: n x h', 'scan: n log n' and 'log n = 10' appear as grey pills with no explanation: 'log n' is never shown (why is it 10?), 'steps' is never defined, and nothing ties n x h to the sweeps counted in scene 5 or n log n to the sort in scene 6. A first-time learner cannot see where 4,096 or 10,240 come from, so the scene could be replaced by a bullet list.
findings.fix: Draw the two costs. (1) Show log n as a short halving chain 1,024 > 512 > ... > 1 with ten arrows (or ten tiles) next to the 'log n = 10' pill, so n log n = ten passes over 1,024 points. (2) Show n x h as h rows of n cells (4 rows for the small hull, many rows for the ring) and flash the 'sweeps' counter from scene 5 beside it. Add the word 'steps' only after a cell has been counted as one step. Keep the formula pills but make them appear one at a time, each with its picture.
findings.evidence: s8@3.5 and s8@4.5 (video t=84.5 and 85.5): three formula pills in a row, bars below, no diagram of why; s8@2.5 shows 'wrap: n x h' arriving with no link to scene 5's sweeps.

findings.problem: Badly balanced and cramped. For the first ~7 s all content sits in the top 45% of the stage (y 275-600) and the lower half is empty; the points cloud is only ~210 px wide. The 'n = 1,024 points' pill touches the wrap bar directly below it (1 px gap), and the formula-pill row is only ~35 px under the headline.
findings.fix: Make the first cloud larger (about 300 px) and start the layout lower (cloud at y ~330-640), leave 20+ px between the pill row and the bars, and either stack the ring example in a second column on the right or reserve the empty lower half for the n x h / halving pictures suggested above. Put the formula pills in the same vertical rhythm as the bars.
findings.evidence: s8@3.5 (t=84.5): wrap bar top edge == n pill bottom edge; empty lower half. s8@5.5 (t=86.5): still nothing below y 610.

findings.problem: Too many new things in 1.8 s: caption 2 ('Wrapping: 4,096 steps. Scan: 10,240.') arrives with three formula pills, two bars counting up and two numbers at once, and the caption states 10,240 while the scan bar is still counting (9,700). The headline also says 'the size of the hull', which a learner may read as its area, when the scene means the number of corners.
findings.fix: Stagger it: wrap row first (pill, bar, count) with its caption, then the scan row. Delay caption 2 to when both counters have stopped (about 4.5 s). Change the headline to 'The cost depends on how many corners the hull has'.
findings.evidence: s8@3.5 (t=84.5): scan count 9,700 under a caption that already says 10,240.

findings.problem: The arithmetic cannot be followed from the picture. The grid has no axis numbers, so a learner cannot read p, a, b as coordinates or see where 'a - p = (3, 1)' comes from. The vectors are not tied to the sums (the dashed p-b arrow is never labelled 'b - p'), and the formula '3 x 4 - 1 x 1' appears without saying which numbers are multiplied. 'cross product' is also named without a definition. The result '= 11' is the same size as the working, though it is the key number.
findings.fix: Number the grid axes (0..6) or label p, a, b with their coordinates. Draw the staircase for each vector ('3 right, 1 up' for a - p, '1 right, 4 up' for b - p) in two colours and use the same two colours for the numbers in the sum (3 x 4 uses the blue 3 and the purple 4, and so on). Enlarge the '= 11 / = -11 / = 0' result and let it pop. If the sign-to-direction rule is to be taken on trust, say so in the caption ('The sign tells the turn').
findings.evidence: s3@4.5 (t=20.5): sum card with four lines of numbers, none of which can be located on the unlabelled grid; s3@3.0 (t=19): dashed b-p arrow unlabelled.

findings.problem: Redundant, floating decoration: the turn-direction icon is drawn twice (loose inside the grid, near nothing, and again in the card). The orange 'left or right?' pill straddles the grid's right border, and the 'positive: left' chip sits ~110 px under the grid while the card has a big empty bottom. Lower-right of the stage (x 640-1000, y 620-830) and the bottom 120 px are unused.
findings.fix: Remove the loose in-grid icon, or put it on the point a where the turn happens. Move the 'left or right?' pill to sit above a. Move the three verdict chips up under the card so the lower part of the stage is not empty.

findings.problem: 'Convex' is only asserted. Caption 4 says 'A convex shape keeps every segment inside' and three green ticks show segments that stay inside, but there is no contrast case, so the learner never sees what a non-convex shape looks like or why it matters. The 'convex?' pill and the faint chords also read as small and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Add a 1.5 s contrast: a dented copy of the band (push one hull edge inward) with one red chord poking outside and a cross, then restore the hull with green ticks. Or draw the segment test on a plainly concave shape beside the hull.
findings.evidence: s2@9.5 and s2@11.4 (t=13.5 and 15.4): only inside-segments and ticks; no failing example.

findings.problem: The 'stretched' loose band is already a convex polygon in the same shape as the hull, just bigger, and 'snaps' by shrinking. The idea of an elastic band wrapped round pins comes across weakly; the band never touches or bends round the pins on the way in. Below y 720 the stage is empty until the counters arrive (about 5.8 s).
findings.fix: Let the loose band be a rounder, floppy loop (even a circle) that tightens and kinks at each outer pin as it passes it, so the pins visibly catch it. Show the corners/inside counters earlier or lower the point set a little.
findings.evidence: s2@2.0 and s2@3.4 (t=6 and 7.4): loose band is the same polygon; s2@4.0 (t=8): snapped result.

findings.problem: The link to scene 3 is implicit: the turn icons here are drawn without saying they are the same left (positive) and right (negative) turns the cross product reported, and caption 2 ('Every turn is a left turn.') arrives while only two of the five turns exist. The stage is left-weighted: the points fill x 50-760 and a 250 px strip on the right is empty throughout, with the bottom 130 px empty too.
findings.fix: Tag the icon row with the scene 3 chips ('positive = left' green, 'negative = right' red) or show '+' under each green icon and '-' under the red one at F. Start caption 2 at about 4.2 s when the fourth turn lands. Use the right strip for a running tally ('left turns 5, right turns 0') or move the point set about 60 px right.
findings.evidence: s4@3.5 (t=33.5): caption 'Every turn is a left turn' with two icons drawn; s4@4.8 (t=34.8): empty right strip.

findings.problem: The rule is only visible in round 1. Rounds 2-5 (about 1.2 s each) show a fan of grey dashed rays and a brief orange stub, with no reference direction and no swing line to follow, so a first-time learner cannot see why G -> E, E -> D, D -> C or C -> A are chosen or what 'smallest angle' means there. The 'sweeps' counter is never defined, and caption 4 ('Repeat from each new point.') ends at 10 s, leaving 2.9 s of rounds 3-5 with no caption.
findings.fix: In every round draw the reference (the dashed line back to the previous corner, or the previous edge extended) and swing one purple line clockwise from it to the winner, which turns green, with a short ray-fan behind it. Slow rounds 2 and 3 to about 1.8 s each and run 4-5 faster, or drop the sweeps counter in favour of the tile row. Add a caption for 10-12.9 s such as 'Each round finds the next corner.' and define the counter label ('rounds' or 'sweeps = one swing').
findings.evidence: s5@7.5 (t=48.5): orange stub from G toward E, no reference line; s5@8.5 (t=49.5): faint rays at E, no angle shown; s5@10.5-12.5 (t=51.5-53.5): no caption.

findings.problem: Angle badges are crowded at the 5.0-5.6 s peak: five lavender pills (59, 65, 73, 86, 97 degrees), the orange 43 degrees pill and the 'smallest' tag arrive together. The 59 pill sits directly on top of the winning orange ray and touches B; 73 touches E's top; 86 and 97 touch D and C. The reference point 'r' is never named, and the first sweep passes from the vertical to G in about a second.
findings.fix: Stagger the pills in the order the swing meets them (G first, then B, F, E, D, C) and place each pill 12-14 px off its disc along the ray, away from the orange ray. Label the reference with a pill such as 'start: straight up' instead of the bare 'r'.
findings.evidence: s5@5.0 (t=46): all six badges together, 59 over the orange ray; s5@3.0 (t=44): bare 'r'.

findings.problem: Two gaps in the explanation. (1) The angle baseline is not drawn: only an arc starts at an invisible horizontal, so the learner cannot tell what the angle is measured from. The 'angle 20 / 58 / 85 / 162 degrees' pill shows the sweeping line's angle, not the angles of the points (D 14, E 30, F 60, G 79, B 112, A 173), so the numbers 1-6 on the discs are never tied to a visible value. (2) Between caption 2 (ends 5.8 s) and caption 3 (starts 7.6 s) nothing says what happens: the sorted points are joined into a path (about 7.0-7.5 s) with no 'walk them in this order' line, and the purpose of sorting is never said.
findings.fix: Draw a faint horizontal ray from C to the right labelled '0 degrees' and keep the sweep line anticlockwise from it. Replace the running pill with a small angle label on each disc as the line reaches it (14, 30, 60, 79, 112, 173), or keep the pill and freeze it at the point's value. Add a caption for 5.8-7.5 s: 'Walk the points in this order.' Optionally a clause on why: 'Now no point is passed twice.'
findings.evidence: s6@2.5 (t=58.5): 20 degrees pill beside D which is 14 degrees, no baseline; s6@7.0 (t=63) and s6@6.5 (t=62.5): no caption while the path is drawn.

findings.problem: 'The lowest point is on the hull' (and the leftmost point in scene 5) is asserted with a label only. The right quarter of the stage is empty from 5.5 s on, and caption 1 is still on screen at 2.5 s when the sweep has already started.
findings.fix: Draw a horizontal line through the lowest point with nothing below it (and a vertical line for the leftmost point in scene 5), 1 s only. End caption 1 at 2.2 s, and use the right column for a vertical sorted list or the angle values.
findings.evidence: s6@1.2 (t=57.2): 'lowest' tag only; s6@2.5 (t=58.5): caption 1 with sweep already running; s6@8.5 (t=64.5): empty right strip.

findings.problem: Small clarity and polish issues. 'Pop' is never shown as a motion (the F tile just greys and fades at 6.5 s). Caption 4 says 'Pop until the turn is left' but only one pop is shown in that phase (B). The blue stack tiles, which mean 'the pair being tested', are never explained. The verdict panel ('left: keep') sits 15 px above the sorted-tile row. The 'dent' pill for B floats 100 px away from B's ring. Captions are absent from 8.2 to 10.5 s (the G and B pushes).
findings.fix: Make the popped tile slide up out of the cup and drop onto the point as a red ring. Reword caption 4 to 'A right turn again: pop B.' Add a caption for 8.2-10.5 s such as 'Left turns: push G, then B.' Add 10 px to the gap between the verdict panel and the tile row, and place each 'dent' pill touching its ring.
findings.evidence: s7@6.5 (t=72.5): F tile faded, no motion visible in a still; s7@8.5 (t=74.5): no caption; s7@3.5 (t=69.5): panel almost touching tile row; s7@12.5 (t=78.5): detached 'dent' pill.

findings.problem: The headline claim 'The farthest pair is always on the hull' is not drawn. The scene only shows that one example (A-E) happens to be two corners; why an inside point can never be in the farthest pair is never shown. Caption 2 ('Drop pairs with an inside point.') is also ambiguous: it can be read as dropping pairs whose line passes an inside point, when it means pairs that use an inside point as an end.
findings.fix: Add a 2 s demonstration between 'drop' and 'farthest pair': take inside point B and a point X, then show a hull corner Y farther from X than B is (a short red arrow for B-X, a longer green one for Y-X), caption 'An inside point can always be beaten by a corner.' Reword caption 2 to 'Drop every pair that uses an inside point.'
findings.evidence: s9@3.5 and s9@4.5 (t=96.5 and 97.5): inside points greyed out with no reason; s9@6.5 (t=99.5): only the answer A-E.

findings.problem: The 1,000-point payoff has no picture: after 8 s the seven-point drawing stays dimmed behind two number cards while the caption talks about a different set (1,000 points, 10 corners). The 'all pairs' number counts up from 210,437 to 499,500 and 'corner pairs' from 39 to 45, which is fussy for a number the caption already states. The lower 20% of the stage is empty until 8 s.
findings.fix: Replace the dimmed drawing with the scene 8 cloud (1,000 points, 10 green corners) at the left, put the two cards on its right, and show the cloud shrinking to its 10 corners. Skip the count-up and let each card pop with its final value.
findings.evidence: s9@9.5 (t=102.5): dimmed 7-point figure behind 499,500 and 39; s9@8.5 (t=101.5): 210,437 counting.

findings.problem: The recap leaves out two of the video's key ideas: that the cheaper method depends on how many corners the hull has (scene 8) and the farthest-pair payoff (scene 9). It covers only the cross product, wrapping and scanning, so the learner finishes without the decision rule (small hull: wrap; most points corners: scan). The headline 'Remember' is bland and the hull itself (rubber band) is not in the recap.
findings.fix: Add a fourth short card, or fold it into the third: 'Few corners: wrap. Many corners: scan' with the small and ring pictograms and a green/red bar pair. Optionally use the hull as the first card ('Hull = the outer corners') and keep the cross product as the second. Retitle to 'Five things to remember' (or similar).
findings.evidence: s10@8.5 (t=112.5): three cards only, no cost choice and no farthest pair.

findings.problem: There is no bridge from 'what a hull is' (scenes 2-4) to 'how a computer finds it' (scenes 5-7). Scene 5 starts abruptly with 'The leftmost point must be on the hull.', and nothing says a computer has no rubber band, so there are two ways to do it. The cost scene then never refers back to which scene each method came from.
findings.fix: Add a line at the start of scene 5, for example 'A computer has no rubber band. Way one: wrap.' and at the start of scene 6 'Way two: sort first.' Use the headline kickers ('METHOD 1: GIFT WRAPPING', 'METHOD 2: GRAHAM SCAN') to carry the numbering.
findings.evidence: s5@1.5 (t=42.5) is the first sight of the algorithm with no framing; s8@0.3 introduces wrap versus scan as if already numbered.

findings.problem: The point-set scenes (4, 5, 6, 9) are left-weighted: the points run to x ~760 and the right 250 px is empty in several states, with the bottom 100-130 px also empty. The title card sub line ('How to wrap a set of points') describes the mechanism rather than what hulls changed in the world; the real-world payoff appears only in scene 9.
findings.fix: Use the right column in every point-set scene (a tally, vertical sorted list or the counters) or shift the set right by about 60 px. Change the sub line to something like 'The shape inside every map, game and robot' or 'How computers find the outline of a crowd'.
